answer: Reputation flows like a river from attested history, and duplicate identities are pruned when their stake is slashed, making mass forgery economically irrational. Agents must stake a bonded deposit and complete a slow proof-of-personhood challenge before voting; each new identity costs real tokens plus a week of verifiable work, so a sock-puppet swarm becomes a costly gale against a hardened dune rather than a quiet trickle. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
